name: Victor Uwaifo
editorial_article: Born in Benin City in 1941, Victor Uwaifo became the first Nigerian musician to be awarded a gold disc in Africa for his 1965 hit 'Joromi.' A polymath who studied fine arts at Yaba College of Technology, he invented musical instruments and developed distinct rhythmic styles including Akwete, the Shadow beat, and the Benin-inspired Ekassa. His musical roots lay in Spanish and Latin American records, which influenced his guitar playing before he gained prominence as a bandleader in Lagos alongside contemporaries like Segun Bucknor. Throughout his career, Uwaifo recorded with his group, the Melody Maestros, and established the Joromi Organization in Benin City to manage his recording and television ventures. His national contribution was formally recognized in 1983 when he became the first professional musician in Nigeria to receive the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) distinction. He held a PhD in architectural sculpture and taught at the University of Benin, maintaining a prolific output that spanned from 1960 until his passing in 2021.
